problemStatement.formal: theorem alternating_triangular_sum : HasSum (fun n : ℕ => if n = 0 then 0 else (-1 : ℝ) ^ (n + 1) * (2 / (↑n * (↑n + 1)))) (4 * Real.log 2 - 2)
problemStatement.plain: Prove the alternating sum of reciprocals of triangular numbers: ∑(-1)^{n+1}·2/(n(n+1)) = 4·ln(2) - 2.
whyMatters: Extends the classical telescoping result ∑2/(n(n+1)) = 2 to its alternating variant
Demonstrates that alternating figurate reciprocals yield transcendental values
Connects triangular numbers to the natural logarithm via the Mercator series

proven: summable_alt_triangular: summability of the alternating series
open: Prove the alternating harmonic series = ln(2) without axioms (requires Abel's theorem)

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: Alternating triangular reciprocals proved (0 sorries, 2 axioms for alternating harmonic series). Gallery entry created. The proof uses partial fractions to split into two Mercator series instances.
builtItems: src/data/proofs/triangular-reciprocals-oq-03/ - Gallery entry with meta.json, annotations.json, index.ts
insights: The shifted alternating harmonic ∑(-1)^{n+1}/(n+1) = 1-ln(2) follows from the standard series by removing first term
HasSum.mul_left and HasSum.sub compose cleanly for combining scaled series
funext + by_cases is the right approach for HasSum function rewriting (not HasSum.congr, which produces finset sum goals)
The alternating sum 4·ln(2)-2 ≈ 0.7726 is transcendental, unlike the non-alternating sum which equals exactly 2
mathlibGaps: Abel's theorem for boundary convergence of power series (needed to prove alternating harmonic series = ln(2))
